transcript:
Header: Stormbridge Payments x Redwood Inference — POC scoping
Date: 2026-06-30 14:00 PDT | Duration: 62m | Recording ID: fb-20260630-8791
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of Platform - Stormbridge), Tomás Rivera (SRE), Priya Kapoor (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros and we'll dive into what success looks like for the POC.
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Lena, I'll be sponsoring this from platform. We have Tomás and Priya with us to dig into telemetry and the models.
[00:15] Tomás Rivera: Hey all.
[00:16] Priya Kapoor: Hi, excited to get this scoped.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Ravi, do you want to kick off with how we typically capture workload topology?
[00:24] Ravi Patel: Yeah, sure. So high level we care about three dimensions: QPS profile (sustained and burst), concurrency distribution (how many concurrent requests at tail percentiles), and token spectrum — input prompt length and generated output length. We also instrument latency quantiles and error mix.
[00:42] Priya Kapoor: For us the tricky bit is we have scheduled batch jobs that spike at end of day plus live auth flows that are small but latency sensitive. So two very different shapes.
[00:53] Maya Chen: Good, can you give ballparks? avg QPS during peak auth?
[00:58] Priya Kapoor: Avg peak auth about 120 qps sustained for 15 minutes, but we see microbursts up to ~700 qps for ~30s on promo days. Batch job windows add an extra 300 qps for a 10 minute window but they're tolerateable if they complete within 60s.
[01:14] Ravi Patel: Okay that's helpful. So for sizing we model the steady auth traffic and the burst layer separately. Key metric for the auth flow is p99 latency under 250ms. For batch, throughput and cost matter more — p90 in 60s is fine.
[01:29] Tomás Rivera: That p99 for auth — is that for end-to-end including our app logic or just inference?
[01:33] Priya Kapoor: We want end-to-end ideally, but for the POC we'll instrument inference alone so we can attribute.
[01:38] Ravi Patel: Right, Redwood can measure inference-only p50/p95/p99. We'll also provide guidance to compute end-to-end using our latency breakdown.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: About token lengths — our fraud signals prompt is very short, 12-40 tokens input and usually 20-60 tokens of output. The customer support rerank flow has long context, up to 2,400 tokens input, output 80-150 tokens.
[02:01] Maya Chen: That's a big spread. For benchmarking we'll want representative percentiles for token length — maybe quantiles at 50/90/99.
[02:08] Priya Kapoor: Yes, and include worst-case long context runs because KV cache impacts latency/cost.
[02:14] Ravi Patel: Agreed. We'll include model variants as well — e.g., full fp32 model and a quantized variant. That lets us show tradeoffs: latency/cost vs quality.
[02:24] Lena Ortiz: On quality, what's the usual pass/fail metric? We can't take any drop in detection rate for fraud.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Good point. Success criteria need to include quality gates per prompt family. Redwood's suggested approach is: define baseline quality from your existing system (e.g., detection precision/recall numbers), then set allowable regression window — typically <1% absolute drop for critical flows, looser for experimental ones.}
[02:46] Priya Kapoor: We can produce baseline evals for the three canonical templates.
[02:50] Ravi Patel: Perfect. For benchmarks we propose a two-phase plan: Phase A — synthetic playback (replay anonymized logs with preserved timing) to validate throughput and SLOs; Phase B — focused end-to-end runs for quality evaluation and manual review. Phase A is a controlled capacity stress test, Phase B is quality gating.
[03:08] Tomás Rivera: About replay — can you run with burst amplification? On promo days we saw superlinear queueing.
[03:14] Ravi Patel: Yep, our synthetic generator can scale burst intensity and inter-arrival distributions. We'll sample real inter-arrival times and then amplify peak factors.
[03:22] Lena Ortiz: Timeline wise, when could we run Phase A?
[03:25] Maya Chen: If we get logs by next Monday and Redwood delivers harness within 48 hours, Phase A could be scheduled the week of 2026-07-13. Does that align?
[03:34] Priya Kapoor: Yes that works. We'll target log export by 2026-07-06.
[03:38] Ravi Patel: For the harness we'll provide a dockerized runner and a spreadsheet with target QPS/concurrency scenarios: steady auth 120 qps, auth microburst 700 qps for 30s, batch steady 300 qps for 10 minutes, and a synthetic long-context profile at lower QPS (15 qps) but heavy tokens.
[03:56] Maya Chen: Let's capture the success criteria explicitly — can we list them?
[04:00] Ravi Patel: Sure. Candidate list: 1) Auth flow inference-only p99 <= 200–250ms for 95% of runs; 2) Batch flow p90 <= 60s; 3) No more than 1% absolute regression in fraud-detection recall on canonical prompt set; 4) Cost estimate within X% of forecast (we'll compute cost per 1M tokens and project); 5) Graceful degradation: when capacity saturated, Redwood gracefully routes to a smaller model variant with documented quality delta.
[04:26] Lena Ortiz: That #[1] p99 target — can you guarantee that on hosted vs dedicated?
[04:31] Ravi Patel: On hosted we'll show baseline numbers but can't guarantee at scale without reserved capacity. For strong p99 SLAs we'd recommend Dedicated capacity or reserved slots for the auth tier. We can model a mixed routing policy: auth on dedicated, batch on burst-dedicated or hosted with surge.
[04:50] Priya Kapoor: Cost model's important — we need token-level cost and a forecast.
[04:54] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize will produce a recommendation and an estimated unit cost matrix per model variant and quantization. We'll deliver a cost projection in the benchmark output.
[05:03] Tomás Rivera: For instrumentation — what telemetry should we pass in headers so you can map tokens to requests?
[05:07] Ravi Patel: Request id, tenant id, model variant, input token count, output token count, and timestamp. Also include a flag for critical flows so we can prioritize in routing.
[05:16] Priya Kapoor: We won't be able to include PII in the payloads. Are anonymized logs fine?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely — anonymized payloads + schema examples are fine. We just need input and output token counts and representative prompt shapes.
[05:29] Ravi Patel: One more thing — tail latency drivers. Long-context runs blow up KV cache miss patterns. We'll instrument cache hit rates; that often explains p99 spikes.
[05:38] Priya Kapoor: We'll provide historical cache/unroll stats from the feature store.
[05:42] Lena Ortiz: Ok on security and compliance — we need SOC2 in writing and an architecture diagram for VPC peering in case we move to Private.
[05:50] Maya Chen: We'll attach our security brief and SOC2 cert. For Private deployment we'll provide network topology and onboarding checklist.
[05:57] Tomás Rivera: For the actual bench runs — will Redwood run them from your hosted fleet or run them in our VPC?
[06:02] Ravi Patel: Initially from Redwood hosted to show typical performance. If you want fidelity we can run the same harness in your VPC in a second phase.
[06:10] Priya Kapoor: Good. What's the expected duration of the POC?
[06:13] Maya Chen: We typically do a 4–6 week engagement: week 0 prepare logs and harness, week 1 Phase A stress runs, week 2 Phase B quality runs and tuning, weeks 3–4 if needed for iteration and commercial pilot negotiation. But can compress if both sides prioritize.
[06:29] Lena Ortiz: That's reasonable. Tomás and I will prioritize log export.
[06:33] Ravi Patel: For the benchmark spreadsheet we'll include: scenario name, target QPS, concurrency expected, token percentile breakdown (p50/p90/p99 input and output), model variant, expected pass criteria, and cost estimate per hour.
[06:47] Priya Kapoor: On model variants — can you enumerate which open models Redwood will test by default?
[06:51] Ravi Patel: We'll propose a small matrix: base open LlamaX-like variant (large), a quantized 4-bit variant, and a smaller low-latency variant. Names may be slightly off in transcript but deliverables will list exact model IDs.
closing_notes: Meeting ended with alignment on deliverables and dates. Redwood to share harness and benchmark spreadsheet; customer to provide logs. Agreed tentative benchmark week of 2026-07-13. Follow-up: Maya to send commercial pilot summary and security docs.
